events.name: Address of the Stockholders of Liberty Hall (pamphlet, November 1866)
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street between Seventh and Eighth, Philadelphia
events.description: Pamphlet, 11 pages, dated November 1866 and published in Philadelphia by Rev. Elisha Weaver; the address read at the dedication of the hall on Nov. 12, 1866. Addressed to 'Fellow Citizens' and signed by ten stockholders: William Whipper, William Still, Rev. Stephen Smith, Robert Allen, William Warrick, Jr., Henry Jones, Rev. J. J. Clinton, Rev. Elisha Weaver, Robert Adger, James W. Purnell. The signers explain that the building was put up for the education of colored youth with funds given and bequeathed by Richard Humphries (as printed) and his associate donors; when the school outgrew it and moved to a larger building, a 'For Sale' placard went up, and they bought it so that it would not 'pass into other hands' and be used 'for base and immoral purposes.' They enlarged it 'in strict conformity with its original design, differing only in this, that the former was for youth, the present, manhood.' They answer objections to the location by arguing for staying in the centre of the community: 'nearly 10,000 of our population are concentrated in 12 or 14 blocks.' They fitted up storerooms in connection with the Hall 'that we may demonstrate the theory of self protection,' urging readers to confine their patronage 'to ourselves and our friends,' and note that 'ten persons combined have in a few short months secured the present structure.' The Hall is dedicated 'to the free discussion of every subject that involves the welfare of mankind.' Note: the Christian Recorder of July 14, 1866 gave the number of stockholders as twelve; the pamphlet has ten. Printed page 9 is missing from the scan read. Source: Charles L. Blockson Afro-American Collection, Temple University Libraries, https://digital.library.temple.edu/digital/collection/p16002coll5/id/2053
attendees: stockholder; signer (Rev.); publisher of the pamphlet

notes: Michiko 2026-11-21: Robert Allen and Henry Jones are kept as their own records (split_appearances.json), here and in Bolivar's 'Purchase and remodeling of Liberty Hall' event. Robert Adger is Robert M. Adger: there is only one.
